chapter: Los Angeles, Central Avenue and the Apex
title: Joining Curtis Moseby's band; Apex Number Two in San Francisco
summary: Royal joins Moseby around 1929, opens the Apex Number Two in San Francisco at about 17, and lists the eleven-piece band's players.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: That was what year, you joined Curtis Moseby's band?

I think it was about 1929. He also was the first guy to ever bring a jazz club to San Francisco, Curtis Moseby was. He bought a place at the corner. He leased a place at the corner of Grant and Bush, which is the exact edge of Chinatown in San Francisco. It was the old Chinese Gardens or something, one of those things, and he leased that place and opened the Apex Number Two in 1929, '30 era and I went up there to open that up the first time I ever left home with a traveling band. We opened the Apex Number Two in, I believe it was 1929 or 1930. 1930 --
Just about. I had my -- let's see, I was 17, yes.
How big a band did Curtis Moseby have?
Oh, 11 pieces or something like that. That was a big band in those days. In those days, when you had three saxaphones, you had a whole lot. We had three
saxophones, four brass and four rhythm. That's 11, that's 11, yes.
Who else was in the band when you joined it? (inaudible)?

When I joined Curtis Moseby's band, there was, let's see, Lawrence Brown was playing trombone. Another very good trumpet player by the name of James Porter and Leo Davis was an alto saxophone player, very good. He was an ex-violin player. A fellow by the name of Johnny Mitchell (PHONETIC) was playing tenor saxophone and I played alto in the band.

Then there was a old Army man, used to play tuba. He was a tuba player in the band. They didn't have bass violin in that band. They had a tuba instead of basses. Army man by the name of Perkins Brookens (PHONETIC). And they had a -- oh, several other fellas that I can't think of in the band at this time, but it was a very good musical band and we played shows. It was a showhouse. They had a very, very good floor show there that included a line of chorus girls, which was my pride and joy, coming up as a young man, and --
They raised me. They showed me what life was all about, good, bad and indifferent, the chorus girls, because I was the baby of every band that I was ever in up until --
